diffusion.label: Bounded logistic diffusion capped by the turnover path
diffusion.comment: Per-district logistic curves (rate, midpoint) are fitted independently to the quarterly adoption share, private battery-electric cars (VEH0142) over private cars (VEH0105), 2011 Q4 to 2025 Q4, recency-weighted. The reported trajectory is the lower, in every predicted quarter, of the district's fitted curve and its own fleet turnover path. The path is a stock-flow model started from the private cars licensed at 2026 Q2 by fuel and year of first registration (VEH9901): cars leave at the scrappage rates observed for British cohorts (VEH1111), cars enter private keepership at the ages at which they do so in each district, new and second hand, and the battery-electric share of new cars rises from 24.7% in 2026 to 80% in 2030 and 100% in 2035 (new pure petrol and diesel car sales end in 2030; every new car is zero emission from 2035). Central scenario: this rule with the scrappage rates of 2021 to 2025. Low: the 2030 level cut to 50%. High: the scrappage rates of 2014 to 2019. Counts are the share multiplied by the district's private cars at 2026 Q2; the petrol and diesel cars remaining, hybrids included, are those cars less the predicted battery-electric cars.
diffusion.stage: Sections 6 and 7 of the companion notebook (export in Section 13)
diffusion.citation: Companion notebook to "Predicting electric vehicle adoption in Wales from open data integrated in semantic knowledge graphs" (manuscript, 2026): EVAdoptionWalesPredictionsModels24Nov.ipynb, export diffusion_scenarios_to_2045.csv.
diffusion.activity_label: Bounded logistic diffusion capped by the fleet turnover path

charging.label: Charging-provision constraint (2045)
charging.comment: Stage 8, research question 2 of the companion notebook. Each LAD's 2045 BEV count from the turnover trajectory is set against public charging devices grown at 5% a year for 20 years ('slow' scenario) and a benchmark of 20 BEVs per public device. LADs that diffuse slowly AND fall short of the benchmark are classed as 'charging plausibly binding'; the rest as 'provision will bind later'. Sensitivity: frozen, slow and sustained (12%/yr) charger growth all leave every LAD below the benchmark. Assumption-driven; not an official forecast.
charging.citation: Companion notebook to "Predicting EV adoption in Wales using Semantic Knowledge Graph" (manuscript, 2026), Stage 8; paper Discussion (charging provision), Stage 8 outputs. Values taken from: companion notebook cell outputs: CLEETS_EV_Adoption_Wales_Quarterly.ipynb.

hierarchical.label: Hierarchical diffusion (two-stage empirical Bayes)
hierarchical.comment: Each district's logistic curve is fitted independently to its adoption share (private battery-electric cars over private cars, 2011 Q4 to 2025 Q4); the fitted midpoint and rate are meta-regressed on standardised population density and population with a DerSimonian-Laird between-district variance, and each district is shrunk towards the value its covariates predict in proportion to its sampling variance. Intervals come from a parametric bootstrap of 300 replicates. The estimates describe the fitted curves before the turnover path is applied.
hierarchical.citation: Companion notebook to "Predicting electric vehicle adoption in Wales from open data integrated in semantic knowledge graphs" (manuscript, 2026): EVAdoptionWalesPredictionsModels24Nov.ipynb, Section 8 of the companion notebook; paper Sections 4.3 and 5.4. Values taken from: hierarchical_midpoints.csv, hierarchical_covariate_effects.csv.

covariates.label: Cross-sectional covariate comparison
covariates.comment: Stages 4a-bis and 5 of the companion notebook (paper S3.4.2, Table 8). Node features per LAD (population, population density, land area; chargers and EV counts are extracted but charger features are excluded from the predictors) are used to predict EVs per 1,000 residents at the target quarter with a mean baseline, Ridge, Random Forest, Extra Trees, GCN, GAT and GraphSAGE under leave-one-out evaluation over the 22 LADs, stochastic models refit under five seeds. The seed spread is at least as large as the gap between the best model and the mean baseline, so no single winning architecture is reported. Ridge residuals rank which LADs adopt above or below what population, density and area alone would predict.
covariates.citation: Companion notebook to "Predicting EV adoption in Wales using Semantic Knowledge Graph" (manuscript, 2026), Stages 4a-bis, 5; paper S3.4.2 (Table 8). Values taken from: companion notebook cell outputs: CLEETS_EV_Adoption_Wales_Quarterly.ipynb.

neural.label: Turnover-constrained neural and graph neural predictions
neural.comment: A multilayer perceptron and a two-layer graph convolutional network over a 22-district similarity graph predict the battery-electric share of the cars that enter private keepership in a district and quarter; the stock follows from the turnover identity, so a prediction cannot grow faster than the entering cars permit (1.48% of the private car stock each quarter, from the turnover model). They are compared with a bounded logistic, a persistence-with-drift baseline and an unconstrained perceptron under one rolling-origin protocol: one quarter ahead for every test quarter from 2022 Q1 to 2025 Q4 (352 district-quarters per model), and rolled forward 1 to 16 quarters from the same origins. The networks are evaluated only; the predictions to 2045 come from the bounded logistic capped by the turnover path.
neural.stage: Sections 9 and 10 of the companion notebook
neural.citation: Companion notebook to "Predicting electric vehicle adoption in Wales from open data integrated in semantic knowledge graphs" (manuscript, 2026): EVAdoptionWalesPredictionsModels24Nov.ipynb, Sections 9 and 10 of the companion notebook; paper Sections 4.4, 4.5 and 5.5; Supplementary Table S8. Values taken from: walk_forward_backtests.csv, multi_horizon_backtest.csv.
neural.activity_label: Turnover-constrained neural and graph neural predictions (model comparison)

turnover.label: Fleet turnover path (observed scrappage and second-hand entry)
turnover.comment: A stock-flow model of private cars by district, fuel and year of first registration, started from the cars licensed at 2026 Q2 (VEH9901). Cars leave at the retention rates observed for British cohorts between year ends (VEH1111; 2021 to 2025 in the central scenario) and are replaced one for one, so each district's private car stock is held at its 2026 Q2 level. Cars enter private keepership at the ages at which they do so in each district, new and second hand, and their battery-electric share follows the sales rule for new cars (24.7% in 2026 rising to 80% in 2030 and 100% in 2035), adjusted for the lower uptake of Welsh private keepers, which converges on the national mix by 2030. The result is a path, an estimate of what the sales rule delivers to the private car stock, and not an upper bound. The Weibull ceiling (14-year median life, every scrapped car replaced by a new one) is kept as a benchmark.
turnover.paper: Sections 4.6 and 5.6 to 5.8; Supplementary Tables S15 to S18
turnover.stage: Sections 6 and 11 of the companion notebook

ontology_terms.comment: A three-month calendar reporting interval.

ontology_terms.subject: https://w3id.org/def/cleets#AdoptionRatioObservation
ontology_terms.label: Electric vehicle adoption-ratio observation
ontology_terms.comment: An observation reporting the relationship between electric vehicle keepership and charging infrastructure.

ontology_terms.subject: https://w3id.org/def/cleets#EVChargerCount
ontology_terms.label: Electric vehicle charger-count observation
ontology_terms.comment: An observation reporting the number of electric vehicle charging devices for an area and reporting period.

ontology_terms.subject: https://w3id.org/def/cleets#EVKeepership
ontology_terms.label: Electric vehicle keepership observation
ontology_terms.comment: An observation reporting the number of registered electric vehicle keepers for an area and reporting period.

ontology_terms.subject: https://w3id.org/def/cleets#EnglishLAD
ontology_terms.label: English local authority district
ontology_terms.comment: A local authority district in England, including unitary authorities, metropolitan and non-metropolitan districts and London boroughs.

ontology_terms.subject: https://w3id.org/def/cleets#IncomeDeprivation
ontology_terms.label: Income-deprivation observation
ontology_terms.comment: An observation reporting an income-deprivation measure for an area and reporting period.

ontology_terms.subject: https://w3id.org/def/cleets#LAD
ontology_terms.label: Local authority district
ontology_terms.comment: A UK local authority district or equivalent administrative area.

ontology_terms.subject: https://w3id.org/def/cleets#ObservableProperty
ontology_terms.label: Observable property
ontology_terms.comment: A property that can be observed in a CLEETS observation.

ontology_terms.subject: https://w3id.org/def/cleets#Population
ontology_terms.label: Population
ontology_terms.comment: Resident population associated with a geographic area.

ontology_terms.subject: https://w3id.org/def/cleets#PopulationDensity
ontology_terms.label: Population Density
ontology_terms.comment: Population per unit area.

ontology_terms.subject: https://w3id.org/def/cleets#WelshLAD
ontology_terms.label: Welsh local authority district
ontology_terms.comment: A principal local authority area in Wales.

ontology_terms.subject: https://w3id.org/def/cleets#quarter
ontology_terms.label: calendar quarter number
ontology_terms.comment: The quarter number of a calendar year.

ontology_terms.subject: https://w3id.org/def/cleets#year
ontology_terms.label: calendar year
ontology_terms.comment: The calendar year associated with a reporting period, as a four-digit integer. xsd:gYear is deliberately avoided: it is outside the OWL 2 datatype map and is rejected by HermiT.

ontology_terms.subject: https://w3id.org/def/cleets#chargerCountValue
ontology_terms.label: charger-count value
ontology_terms.comment: The number of electric vehicle charging devices reported by a charger-count observation.

ontology_terms.subject: https://w3id.org/def/cleets#chargersPerKeeper
ontology_terms.label: chargers-per-keeper value
ontology_terms.comment: The number of charging devices divided by the number of electric vehicle keepers for the same area and period. Reciprocal of cleets:keeperChargerRatio and recorded only where a source reports it directly.

ontology_terms.subject: https://w3id.org/def/cleets#densityValue
ontology_terms.label: densityValue
ontology_terms.comment: Population density in persons per square kilometre.

ontology_terms.subject: https://w3id.org/def/cleets#hasSimpleResult
ontology_terms.label: has simple result
ontology_terms.comment: Links an observation to a literal result value.

ontology_terms.subject: https://w3id.org/def/cleets#deprivationDecile
ontology_terms.label: income-deprivation decile
ontology_terms.comment: The decile assigned to an area by the relevant deprivation index, where 1 denotes the most deprived tenth.

ontology_terms.subject: https://w3id.org/def/cleets#incomeDeprivationValue
ontology_terms.label: income-deprivation value
ontology_terms.comment: A numeric income-deprivation value reported for an area.

ontology_terms.subject: https://w3id.org/def/cleets#keeperChargerRatio
ontology_terms.label: keepers-per-charger value
ontology_terms.comment: The number of electric vehicle keepers divided by the number of charging devices for the same area and period.

ontology_terms.subject: https://w3id.org/def/cleets#keepershipValue
ontology_terms.label: keepership value
ontology_terms.comment: The number of registered electric vehicle keepers reported by a keepership observation.

ontology_terms.subject: https://w3id.org/def/cleets#ladCode
ontology_terms.label: local authority district code
ontology_terms.comment: The official statistical code assigned to a local authority district, for example W06000015.

ontology_terms.subject: https://w3id.org/def/cleets#populationValue
ontology_terms.label: populationValue
ontology_terms.comment: Population count.

ontology_terms.subject: https://w3id.org/def/cleets#yearQuarter
ontology_terms.label: year-quarter label
ontology_terms.comment: A human-readable year-quarter label, such as 2025-Q4.

ontology_terms.subject: https://w3id.org/def/cleets#forLAD
ontology_terms.label: for local authority district
ontology_terms.comment: Links a CLEETS observation to the local authority district to which it applies. Functional: an observation reports one district.

ontology_terms.subject: https://w3id.org/def/cleets#forTime
ontology_terms.label: for observation period
ontology_terms.comment: Links a CLEETS observation to its temporal reporting period. Functional: an observation reports one period.

ontology_terms.subject: https://w3id.org/def/cleets#hasFeatureOfInterest
ontology_terms.label: has feature of interest
ontology_terms.comment: Links an observation to the entity whose property is observed.

ontology_terms.subject: https://w3id.org/def/cleets#hasPopulation
ontology_terms.label: hasPopulation
ontology_terms.comment: Links an area to its population.

ontology_terms.subject: https://w3id.org/def/cleets#hasPopulationDensity
ontology_terms.label: hasPopulationDensity
ontology_terms.comment: Links an area to its population density.

ontology_terms.subject: https://w3id.org/def/cleets#observedProperty
ontology_terms.label: observed property
ontology_terms.comment: Links an observation to the property that was observed.

ontology_terms.subject: https://w3id.org/def/cleets#observesProperty
ontology_terms.label: observes property
ontology_terms.comment: Links a CLEETS observation to the property being observed.

ontology_terms.subject: https://w3id.org/def/cleets#phenomenonTime
ontology_terms.label: phenomenon time
ontology_terms.comment: Links an observation to the time to which the result applies.

activity.label: Bounded logistic diffusion capped by the fleet turnover path
activity.comment: Per-district logistic curves (rate, midpoint) are fitted independently to the quarterly adoption share, private battery-electric cars (VEH0142) over private cars (VEH0105), 2011 Q4 to 2025 Q4, recency-weighted. The reported trajectory is the lower, in every predicted quarter, of the district's fitted curve and its own fleet turnover path. The path is a stock-flow model started from the private cars licensed at 2026 Q2 by fuel and year of first registration (VEH9901): cars leave at the scrappage rates observed for British cohorts (VEH1111), cars enter private keepership at the ages at which they do so in each district, new and second hand, and the battery-electric share of new cars rises from 24.7% in 2026 to 80% in 2030 and 100% in 2035 (new pure petrol and diesel car sales end in 2030; every new car is zero emission from 2035). Central scenario: this rule with the scrappage rates of 2021 to 2025. Low: the 2030 level cut to 50%. High: the scrappage rates of 2014 to 2019. Counts are the share multiplied by the district's private cars at 2026 Q2; the petrol and diesel cars remaining, hybrids included, are those cars less the predicted battery-electric cars.

scenarios.comment: 2030 level cut to 50% (the lowest option of the 2026 mandate review). Each district follows the lower of its fitted diffusion curve and its turnover path. The Wales path is 75.32% of private cars at 2045 Q4, the predicted Wales share is 75.32% and Wales reaches 50% in 2040 Q1.

Legislated sales rule, scrappage rates of 2021 to 2025. Each district follows the lower of its fitted diffusion curve and its turnover path. The Wales path is 81.14% of private cars at 2045 Q4, the predicted Wales share is 81.14% and Wales reaches 50% in 2038 Q2.

Scrappage rates of 2014 to 2019. Each district follows the lower of its fitted diffusion curve and its turnover path. The Wales path is 88.35% of private cars at 2045 Q4, the predicted Wales share is 88.35% and Wales reaches 50% in 2037 Q1.
